headline: Legal liability gap emerges as AI agents operate without accountability
body: Experts are raising critical questions about who bears responsibility when AI agents cause harm, with current legal frameworks leaving a dangerous accountability void. For healthcare organizations deploying AI in clinical decision-making, EHR integration, and patient care workflows, this gap creates immediate compliance and malpractice exposure. Healthcare systems cannot rely on vendor indemnification or agent autonomy as shields against liability when these tools influence diagnoses, treatment plans, or billing decisions. This legal ambiguity means healthcare AI implementation now requires explicit governance structures, audit trails, and human oversight protocols that vendors and health systems must establish proactively. The consulting and procurement landscape will shift as risk management becomes inseparable from AI adoption strategy.
